notes.claim: Even older students often think additively by default, and common ratio mistakes come from focusing on a constant difference where a multiplicative comparison is needed.
A scale of 1 cm on a drawing for 1 metre in real life is a scale of 1 : 100, and both measurements need the same units to write the ratio.
A reduction gear definition from a marine engine maker: gearboxes transfer power from a drive shaft to a driven shaft and reduce speed.

sources.title: Reduction gear, gearbox, Wartsila Encyclopedia
sources.quote: Gearboxes consist of meshing teeth on pinions and wheels which transfer power from a drive shaft to a driven shaft and reduce speed.

sources.title: Scale drawings, KS3 Maths, BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: For example, 1 cm on a scale drawing representing 1 metre in real life is a scale of 1 : 100

sources.title: Map scales and ratio, KS3 Maths, BBC Bitesize
sources.quote: In order to write the ratio, both measurements need to have the same units.

sources.title: Introducing multiplicative thinking, NCETM
sources.quote: Any secondary teacher will tell you that even older students often think additively by default.

sources.title: Second-Year Pre-Service Teachers' Responses to Proportional Reasoning Test Items, ERIC
sources.quote: common mistakes in ratio and proportion are often the result of a focus on constant difference when multiplicative comparisons are more appropriate
